method: Surfaced via raw-ingest triage (cnbc-technology.json, gnews-ai-litigation.json this cycle -- Meta Q2 2026 earnings, reported same day). Business claim type throughout. Given the ~30-minute cycle window, verified directly against the Tier-0 primary source (Meta Investor Relations Q2 2026 press release) via WebFetch, cross-checked against two independent financial-news outlets (StockTitan, Investing.com) rather than spinning separate verifier/falsifier sub-agents. dedup-check clean, no archive match.
origin_items: cnbc-technology.json: 'Meta reports second-quarter results after the close', 'Meta's Reality Labs lost over $4.6 billion in second quarter'; gnews-ai-litigation.json: 'Meta misses profit expectations, sticks to massive AI spending' (The Guardian), 'Meta shares tumble 10%' (New York Post), 'Meta's Profit Falls 14% as A.I. Spending Continues' (NYT), all 2026-07-29.

claims.text: Meta reported Q2 2026 revenue of $60.8 billion (up 28% year over year) and net income of $15.8 billion (down 14% year over year), with diluted EPS of $6.18, missing the average analyst estimate of $7.17
claims.reasoning: Revenue/net income figures directly from Meta's own Q2 2026 press release (Tier-0 primary, WebFetch). EPS and analyst-estimate figures corroborated independently by StockTitan and Investing.com (both fetched directly, not from search snippets alone).

claims.text: Q2 2026 capital expenditure was $31.08 billion, more than double the $17.0 billion spent in Q2 2025; Meta narrowed its full-year 2026 capex guidance to $130-145 billion from a prior $125-145 billion range
claims.reasoning: Capex figure and the 'narrowed from $125-145B' detail both directly from Meta's own release, independently matched by StockTitan and Investing.com's earnings-call transcript coverage (which also carried CFO Susan Li's on-record framing of the guidance).

claims.text: Meta's Reality Labs division posted an operating loss of $4.62 billion in Q2 2026 on revenue of $431 million, up from $370 million a year earlier
claims.reasoning: Directly from Meta's own release, matched by StockTitan's independent restatement of the same figures.

claims.text: Meta shares fell about 9.6% in after-hours trading following the release
claims.reasoning: Market-reaction figure (9.64%, $585.61 to $529.15) fetched live from Investing.com across two separate articles (slides summary and earnings-call transcript), both consistent. Not in Meta's own release (Meta does not report its own stock price). Headline direction (a sell-off) is also independently corroborated by New York Post ('shares tumble 10%') and BBC ('Meta shares fall') per this cycle's raw ingest, though those two were not independently re-fetched given the cycle time window -- flagged as a minor gap, not used as numbered sources.

claims.text: CFO Susan Li said the narrowed capex guidance reflects a focus on 'maximizing 2026 and 2027 capacity' while preserving flexibility for later years; CEO Mark Zuckerberg said Meta continues 'to invest aggressively in infrastructure to meet the demand'
claims.reasoning: Direct quotes carried in Investing.com's earnings-call transcript coverage. Zuckerberg's separate quote in Meta's own press release ('AI is accelerating our core business today...') is consistent in tone but is a different quote from the same call/release; the transcript-sourced quotes used in the article are attributed only to Investing.com's transcript.

falsifier_notes: No separate adversarial falsifier sub-agent run this cycle given the ~30-minute window; verification was done directly against the Tier-0 primary source (Meta's own earnings release) plus two independently fetched financial-news outlets (StockTitan, Investing.com) that were cross-checked against each other and found consistent on every figure used. No dispute or contradiction found. Known gap: the specific 9.6% after-hours stock-drop figure rests on one outlet (Investing.com, cited twice/two articles) rather than two fully independent outlets; direction of the move (a sell-off) is independently corroborated by NYT/NY Post/BBC/Guardian headlines seen in raw ingest but not re-fetched for time. Not treated as load-bearing enough to block publication given it is descriptive market context, not the story's central claim.
